claims.scope: Cultivated Asian edible gall association
claims.statement: Edible jiaobai gall tissue involves Zizania latifolia associated with Ustilago esculenta.
limits: Does not establish infection in any North American native Zizania species.
Does not establish environmental transmission from retailed food.
claims.source_locator: Tu 2019 PubMed abstract and Chigira 2023 introduction: Z. latifolia galls contain U. esculenta

claims.scope: Riverside County, California, introduced host, November 2017
claims.statement: CDFA reported PCR and sequencing detection of Ustilago esculenta in introduced Zizania latifolia tissue.
limits: This is not a native manoomin detection.
Does not show current establishment.
claims.source_locator: CDFA 2017 pest-rating account, sample identification in Riverside County

claims.scope: 2019 Japanese study: five harvested galls at differing swelling stages; laboratory isolation
claims.statement: Tu et al. reported culturing several Ustilago esculenta strains from harvested Zizania latifolia galls.
limits: Culturing U. esculenta from gall tissue establishes recoverability at sampling, not infectious competence, spores at retail, or viability after shipping.
Five sampled galls at different swelling stages do not estimate the prevalence of viable fungus in the U.S. retail food supply.
claims.source_locator: Tu 2019 abstract: five harvested swollen-gall samples, isolates identified by DNA sequencing; not a post-shipment challenge

claims.scope: Cultivated Japanese white versus gray gall stages
claims.statement: Chigira et al. distinguish white edible galls and gray galls containing mature teliospores.
limits: Edible white tissue can contain fungal mycelium even without visible mature spore-bearing sori.
Strain-level infectivity and life-cycle differences matter; color is not a validated diagnostic test for a retail consignment.
claims.source_locator: Chigira 2023 introduction: M-T edible white galls with low sorus formation, T gray galls with abundant sori

claims.scope: EPPO synthesis of established introduced plant populations, including Hawaii and British Columbia
claims.statement: EPPO reports introduced Zizania latifolia populations in Hawaii and British Columbia and wetland invasion effects.
limits: This is evidence about the plant, not a native-host fungal outbreak.
EPPO regulatory listing is not U.S. import law.
claims.source_locator: EPPO 2024 datasheet distribution and impact summary, a regulatory-region synthesis

claims.scope: California agency assessment in 2018
claims.statement: CDFA's 2018 assessment said imports of Zizania latifolia stems were prohibited at that time.
limits: Does not establish the current 2026 federal status of fresh or processed food products.
claims.source_locator: CDFA Z. latifolia assessment dated 2018; historical stated restriction, not current federal advice

claims.scope: 2025 Wisconsin Tribal Conservation Advisory Council and DATCP manoomin survey
claims.statement: Wisconsin DATCP describes a 2025 tribal-directed manoomin survey addressing other pathogens.
limits: Not evidence of Ustilago esculenta presence or absence.
Does not grant outside field access or governance authority.
claims.source_locator: DATCP Plant Industry Bureau Laboratory webpage, WTCAC 2025 study description and named survey targets

claims.scope: October 2026 Reddit report, no direct independent item examination by 561
claims.statement: A Reddit participant reported observing U.S. retail jiaobai and said they reported observations to USDA.
limits: Not an independently verified product identity, importer record, rule violation or biological sample.
claims.source_locator: Public October 2026 Reddit account: author describes sightings and having contacted USDA; no independent chain of custody

claims.scope: Fresh cut edible stems from China, imported for consumption in 2026
claims.statement: The current commodity-specific U.S. admissibility determination was not available to this review.
limits: APHIS general commodity guidance is not a Zizania-specific approval or denial.
Do not accuse stores based on this unresolved question.
claims.source_locator: APHIS commodity approval guide gives the process, not a Zizania-specific import ruling

claims.species: Zizania aquatica, Zizania palustris, Zizania texana
claims.scope: Modern North American native Zizania, no confirmed direct host record in reviewed set
claims.statement: The reviewed sources do not resolve modern native-host susceptibility or establish an actual native-bed infection.
limits: An uncertain host range is not proof of resistance or infection.
A secondary agency list is not a directly verified native diagnosis.
claims.source_locator: CDFA 2017 species list; CDFA 2018 botanist commentary; primary native host diagnosis missing from reviewed corpus

claims.species: Ustilago esculenta on cultivated Zizania latifolia
claims.scope: 2017 Chinese study of Longjiao 2 cultivar, two selected sexually compatible pairs of T and MT isolates, laboratory and greenhouse conditions
claims.statement: Zhang et al. (2017) observed T-type isolates from gray galls with more complete mating/infection and teliospore development than MT-type isolates from edible white galls; the tested MT isolates showed impaired infection and germination.
claims.source_locator: Zhang et al. 2017, PMC5719756, Abstract Results/Conclusion and infection assays; compare tested isolate pairs, not all field strains
limits: The assay tested specific isolates under laboratory/greenhouse conditions on Asian Z. latifolia; no American Zizania host was tested.
Impaired infection for MT isolates does not prove complete noninfectiousness of every edible gall or every strain during all possible exposures.
This study does not assay imported market products or occurrence in North American habitats.

claims.scope: USFWS April 2025 Ecological Risk Screening Summary, contiguous-US climate match and global invasion history
claims.statement: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service classified Zizania latifolia as High Risk based on demonstrated invasive history and broad contiguous-U.S. establishment climate match.
claims.source_locator: USFWS ERSS public summary, risk category, establishment climate matching and described history of invasiveness
limits: The high-risk screening result is a potential establishment risk, not a documented local manoomin-bed displacement or a state/federal prohibitory rule.
The conclusion concerns the introduced plant's ecological invasion risk; it does not establish U. esculenta host switching.

claims.scope: US retail edible stems from specified foreign origin, postharvest transport, disposal and exposure
claims.statement: Neither the presence of an infectious T-type strain nor the viability of a transmissible life stage after real food-distribution conditions has been established for the reported U.S. retail observations.
claims.source_locator: Contrast Zhang 2017 isolate-specific infection assays and Tu 2019 harvest isolation with missing shipment-specific retail sample and plant-health determination
limits: No conclusion of pathogen absence is justified by a missing commercial shipment assay.
No claim of infectious retail inoculum is justified by culturing an unrelated harvested gall.

claims.scope: 2017 controlled cross mating/inoculation study on Asian cultivar Longjiao 2
claims.statement: In Zhang et al. 2017, some T-type and MT-type fungal isolate combinations mated and produced successful infection in Asian Z. latifolia despite the tested MT/MT pair's infection defect.
claims.source_locator: Zhang et al. 2017 PMC5719756 Discussion, paragraph beginning 'Additionally, the sporidia from the T and MT strains could mate with each other'; Figures 5–6
limits: This is a cross among selected isolates in experimental conditions, not measured mixing or infection of actual market produce.
It invalidates an unconditional assumption that all MT-bearing material is unable to contribute to infection; it does not establish host compatibility with native American wild rice.

claims.scope: Comparison of fungus-maintained edible cultivars with wild or introduced populations of the same plant species
claims.statement: Artificially maintained edible jiaobai cultivars are propagated using infected rhizomes and lose flowering, while Z. latifolia as a plant species can reproduce and disperse via rhizomes and, in some settings, viable seeds.
claims.source_locator: Guo 2015 Summary/Introduction on crop selection; USFWS 2025 ERSS pp.2, 4–5 ecology; NZ MPI eradication webpage on seed and fragment spread
limits: Inferring that an edible cultivar typically fails to set seed does not establish all wild/introduced Z. latifolia are sterile.
The extent of seed-based establishment depends on locality and cultivar; no site-specific North American field estimate is supplied.

claims.scope: New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries: National Interest Pest Responses programme and site management
claims.statement: New Zealand's biosecurity authority documents established Z. latifolia infestations and an active national eradication/containment programme, including an approximately 500-hectare Northland infestation area.
claims.source_locator: MPI 'Where manchurian wild rice has been found in NZ' and 'control and eradication' sections
limits: New Zealand's Biosecurity Act restrictions do not create corresponding U.S. import prohibitions.
Reported treatment duration and area are programme context, not a measured risk to any named American manoomin bed.

claims.scope: USFWS April 2025 risk summary quoting Terrell and Batra 1982 historical U.S. planting records
claims.statement: USFWS 2025 summarizes an older report of U.S. introduced living Z. latifolia plantings at federal research facilities and transfers to university researchers, separate from edible-stem retail reports.
claims.source_locator: Full ERSS first two PDF pages, Status in United States; 1982 Terrell and Batra passage quoted, including Patuxent and University of Minnesota research transfer
limits: These are historical plantings described in a 1982 account and repeated in a 2025 screening, not evidence those facilities still maintain them.
A living research planting is a distinct category from contemporary imported cut vegetable products.

claims.scope: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission public Manoomin stewardship programme
claims.statement: GLIFWC describes a manoomin stewardship programme guided by Tribal rice chiefs, elders and member nations' natural-resource departments, connecting traditional ecological knowledge with scientific research on decline and habitat.
claims.source_locator: GLIFWC 'Ganawenindiwag Manoomin Anishinaabeg' public programme description, opening paragraphs and Habitat Requirements
limits: Public programme description does not constitute partnership or permission to disclose Traditional Ecological Knowledge and protected rice-bed locations.
Climate and water pollution pressures are active steward priorities, not evidence of U. esculenta presence.

claims.scope: Wisconsin DNR published 2026-10-07 Wild Rice Stewardship Council summit agenda
claims.statement: Wisconsin DNR published an October 7, 2026 council summit agenda with State/Tribal Technical Committee updates, review of priorities, and discussion of possible partners.
claims.source_locator: Wisconsin DNR 2026-09-10 event page: 2026-10-07 agenda items 1:30–2:45 p.m.
limits: An announced agenda does not verify that the summit occurred as planned or that any resolution or partnership was adopted.
No assumption of invitation or endorsement of 561 Group research is justified.

claims.scope: 2026 Fond du Lac Band, Minnesota Land Trust and DNR proposed Cedar Lake manoomin restoration
claims.statement: Minnesota DNR described a proposed project with the Fond du Lac Band and Minnesota Land Trust to restore water levels favorable to manoomin at Cedar Lake; the EAW public comment deadline was August 27, 2026.
claims.source_locator: Minnesota DNR 2026-07-28 press release, project description and comment deadline
limits: A proposal and past comment period are not proof the project was approved, funded, or completed.
Protected on-reservation restoration access is not permission for outside environmental observation or intervention.

claims.scope: Inspection of the enumerated federal noxious-weed taxa in 7 CFR 360.200 as of 2026-10-11
claims.statement: Zizania latifolia does not appear by name in the examined enumerated taxa of the federal noxious-weed list at 7 CFR 360.200.
claims.source_locator: 7 CFR 360.200, aquatic/wetland, parasitic and terrestrial weed lists; complete named-taxon search for 'Zizania' on 2026-10-11
limits: Absence from this named federal noxious-weed list is not an import approval, and other laws, import orders, or state rules can apply.
This is a legal-text observation, not a commodity-specific APHIS admissibility determination for China-origin jiaobai.

release_gates.note: Do not derive a store-violation report, outbreak warning or accepted scientific release from this dataset without current primary receiving evidence and appropriate authority.

source_notes: Evidence statuses describe what source texts support in their own host/material context, not independent scientific acceptance, measured contemporary risk, or official U.S. commodity compliance. Sources may reference overlapping scientific study populations; event identifiers must not be treated as counts of independent infected plants. Added source-critical differentiators: partial MT infection phenotype is not a categorical safety rule because some T/MT mixed pairings infected cultivated Asian hosts; FWS 2025 documents old living-plant research introductions; NZ live-plant management differs from US food import status. Existing stewardship plans are public, not external consent.
